teaser.text: To understand WuXi AppTec, follow a medicine from an idea to a factory and then follow the money through that journey. WuXi sells the scientific work, testing, development and manufacturing that drug companies need, while its economics depend on turning that work into repeat orders at a profit.

blocks.heading: Does WuXi’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The cash position improved substantially after that investment phase. Free cash flow reached RMB10,600.072 million in 2025, allowing WuXi to fund dividends and share purchases more comfortably. Even so, payouts can exceed free cash flow when a company also uses existing cash, debt, asset sales or new equity.

Free cash flow was RMB10,600.072 million after capital spending, lease payments and interest. After RMB801.758 million of stock pay, real free cash flow was RMB9,798.314 million. Stock pay does not use cash immediately, but it gives employees part of the business’s value, so deducting it gives an owner-oriented view.

paragraphs.text: Base dividends rise from CNY2.70 per share to CNY3.15 and CNY3.66. The path uses the analyst EPS estimate of CNY9.032 and the board’s 30% payout policy, followed by moderate earnings growth. Bear dividends fall to CNY1.30 and then remain near CNY1.20 because weaker earnings and investment needs could reduce the payout. Bull dividends reach CNY2.85, CNY3.60 and CNY4.50 if demand and utilization sustain stronger EPS.

blocks.heading: What is WuXi’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The dividend yield is 1.1%, so investors depend mainly on future growth. Enterprise value is 9.2 times revenue, while price to book is 6.1 times. That means the market expects customer relationships, scientific expertise, and new capacity to produce much more than the accounting assets alone.

earnings.title: WuXi earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: WuXi reports on October 26, 2026; guidance points to revenue growth, cash generation and backlog conversion.
earnings.opening: WuXi's next results are expected on October 26, 2026. For WuXi, the key watch is whether backlog converts into cash as new capacity becomes productive.
earnings.closing: The full memo answers how WuXi's business works, who its rivals are, how WuXi is managed, and what risks it faces.

paragraphs.text: Management guides 2026 total revenue to RMB58,500–60,500 million and continuing-operations growth to 35.0%–39.0%. It expects capital spending of RMB7,500–8,500 million and adjusted free cash flow of RMB13,500–14,500 million. TIDES revenue is expected to grow 45.0%; TIDES develops and makes peptide and oligonucleotide medicines.

blocks.heading: Did WuXi deliver on its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast revenue of RMB41.5–43.0 billion in March 2025. Actual revenue was RMB45.46 billion. It also proposed a RMB1.0 billion interim dividend in March 2026, while the eventual distribution reached RMB1.51 billion. Those are credible delivery signals, but the final test is whether growth leaves more cash and earning power behind each share after compensation, financing and insider selling.

blocks.heading: What do WuXi's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 55.2% from the year-earlier June quarter. Gross margin rose from 46.6% to 55.8%. Chemistry remained the main engine, but first-half small-molecule development and manufacturing grew faster than TIDES, so the acceleration broadened beyond the previous year’s peptide and oligonucleotide surge.

blocks.heading: What should WuXi watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The October 26, 2026 nine-month results will test guidance, customer payments and backlog conversion. Middletown and Couvet, followed by Singapore and Taixing, will test whether commissioning and customer qualification turn expansion into productive capacity. Couvet’s spray-drying facility is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and Singapore production in 2027. Programme progression, site utilization, cash generation and customer decisions during 2027–2028 will decide whether margins and valuation hold.
